D013_m001.question:
I’ve been feeling... off… for about five months now. Ever since the night shift got quieter—just me and the echoes in the hallways. I used to manage, but now it’s hard just to stand up, let alone walk my rounds. Everything feels heavier. My body moves like it’s underwater. 

I cry sometimes—too much. Can’t stop it. Doesn’t even take much to set me off. I sit in the security booth and just… break down. 

Lately, I’ve been thinking… maybe it’s my fault she died. My wife. That I didn’t see it coming. That I didn’t do enough. Now I think maybe I caused it somehow—like I brought the illness into the house. Sometimes I wonder if bad things happen wherever I go. The power went out at the station last week? I thought, *That’s me. Another thing on me.*

I can’t sleep, not really. I just lie there, thinking. A few weeks ago, I filled a pill bottle—my blood pressure meds—emptied everything into my hand and stared. I didn’t do it. But I wanted to. I wrote a note and burned it in the sink.

I can’t keep going like this. I can’t focus. Can’t remember things. I called in sick twice last month—the first time in twenty years. I’m not who I used to be.
D013_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m002.question:
I’ve just turned 23, and for the past five months, things have felt… heavy. I used to find peace in ballet—my body moving exactly as it should, every step precise. But now, even getting out of bed feels impossible. Some days, I cry for no reason, curled up on the floor of my dressing room before rehearsal. My limbs feel like they’re made of lead, and I can’t keep up. My movements are slow, even offstage. I fumble when I tie my pointe shoes.

I keep thinking it’s all my fault—that somehow, my not being good enough caused my dad’s accident last winter, even though it happened miles from home. I replay it constantly, like if I’d called him that night, maybe… it’s irrational, I know, but it feels true.

I miss dancing, but I also can’t stand seeing myself in the mirror. I’ve thought about ending it—specifically, taking my dad’s old prescription when no one’s home, maybe next weekend. I used to have so much control, but now I just feel broken. I’ve missed six weeks of performances. My director’s concerned. I don’t know who I am without this.
D013_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m003.question:
I’ve just felt… heavy… for about five months now. It started around winter semester—I was supposed to teach two courses, but I couldn’t get out of bed most mornings. Just getting dressed takes so much effort, like my body’s made of concrete. I walk slower, talk slower. My wife noticed I keep staring into space during dinner.  

The worst part is this constant weight of guilt. I keep thinking that if I’d just been a better person—better father, better professor—then maybe that student last semester wouldn’t have dropped out. Or that my colleague wouldn’t have had that accident driving home after our meeting. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t shake it—like I’m somehow the reason bad things happen.  

Some days, when I’m on the third floor of the engineering building, I get this sudden urge to step over the railing. It’s not that I want to die, not really—it's more like my body tenses up, and for a split second, I feel pulled toward the edge. Then I snap back and hold the railing tighter.  

I haven’t told anyone until now. I used to take pride in my work—now I can’t focus long enough to grade a quiz. My wife asks if I’m okay, but I don’t even know how to answer.
D013_m003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m004.question:
I’ve just felt… empty for about the past five months. It started slowly—just not wanting to get out of bed, then not caring about school or hanging out with friends. Now it’s like I can’t shake this heavy sadness no matter what. Some days I just sit on the edge of my bed, picking at the skin around my nails until it bleeds, too restless to lie down but too tired to do anything. I pace my room a lot, especially at night.

At work, I review graphic footage all day—accidents, violence, stuff most people would never see. I keep thinking I should be stronger, that I shouldn’t be this affected. I replay moments—like the time I missed a flagged video, or when I snapped at my sister for no reason—and I can’t let it go. I keep telling myself I’m failing at everything. What’s wrong with me?

Lately… I’ve started thinking maybe it would just be easier if I weren’t here. Not because I want to hurt myself, but because I feel like I’m just breaking everything I touch. I don’t have a plan or anything, but the thought comes a lot—like a quiet voice that won’t leave. I can’t focus on assignments, and I’ve stopped going out. I just don’t see the point sometimes.
D013_m004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m005.question:
I’ve been the captain of cargo ships for over thirty years—spent more time at sea than on land some years. But these past five months, something’s changed. I don’t feel like myself. I don’t feel anything, really. Just... empty. It’s like the compass inside me stopped working. When my wife talks to me, I know she’s asking how I am, but I sit there, quiet, because the words take too long to come out. I don’t mean to ignore her. I just can’t get my thoughts to move fast enough.

I keep thinking about old decisions—times I rerouted late, delays I caused, the crew I may have pushed too hard. Small things, years ago, but they run through my head every night like a broken echo. I should’ve done better. I should’ve been better.

Most days, I don’t want to get out of bed. Even the sea, the rhythm of the ship—it doesn’t calm me like it used to. Some mornings, I think it’d just be easier if I didn’t wake up at all. I wouldn’t act on it—I won’t do that to my wife—but the thought doesn’t leave me. I used to command a vessel through storms. Now I can’t command myself to shower in the morning.
D013_m005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m006.question:
Lately… it's been really hard to get through the day. For the past two months, I’ve just felt empty, like a switch flipped and I can’t find my way back. I used to love coming into the gym—coaching people, staying sharp—but now I’ll show up and just stand there, zoning out, forgetting clients’ names or what set we were on. I sleep a lot, like 10, 12 hours a night, and still feel exhausted. Sometimes I nap after work, even though I know I should be active. Honestly, I’ve stopped caring.  

I’ve even thought about… ending things. Not just "I wish I wasn’t here," but how I’d do it—like, I’ve figured out when and where no one would find me for a while. I keep it to myself, but it’s there, all the time.  

It’s affecting everything. I’ve had to cut back on shifts because I can’t focus, and guys I train have noticed I’m off—quiet, slow to respond. I don’t call friends anymore. My apartment’s a mess. I used to take pride in staying disciplined, in being strong for others. Now I can’t even take care of myself.
D013_m006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m007.question:
I’ve just turned 51, and for the past two months, things that used to feel manageable now seem impossible. As a head nurse, I’ve always prided myself on being sharp—knowing meds, catching changes in patients before anyone else—but lately, I walk into a room and forget why I’m there. I’ll set down my keys or phone and spend ten minutes looking for them. It’s not just forgetfulness; it’s like my mind is foggy, like I’m not really *here*.  

Sleep’s been awful. I wake up around 3 or 4 most nights and just lie there. My brain won’t shut off, but not with real thoughts—just this hollow silence. That’s how I feel most of the time: empty. I don’t cry much. I don’t feel much of anything. I go through the motions at work, but I know I’m not as present as I should be. The staff’s noticed.  

Honestly, some mornings I wish I didn’t wake up. Not because I want to end things—no plans or anything—but because the idea of facing another day like this just feels… too heavy. I used to find meaning in helping others. Now, I’m not sure I can help myself.
D013_m007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m008.question:
Lately, I just feel… stuck. For the past two months, it’s like I’m moving through fog. I wake up after eight hours and still feel exhausted—like my body’s heavy, my head’s full of static. It doesn’t matter how much I sleep; I’m never refreshed. Work used to be my thing—building features, debugging, even late-night coding marathons—but now I stare at the screen and can’t focus. I used to love choosing what to work on, but now I’ll sit there for ten minutes trying to decide whether to open my email or my IDE. It’s ridiculous, right? Even picking what to eat or what shirt to wear feels impossible.

I canceled plans with friends, not because I don’t want to see them, but because getting up, showering, just… starting anything takes so much effort. I’ve missed deadlines. My manager checked in, and I didn’t know what to say. The truth is, I’ve thought about not being here. A few weeks ago, I filled a bottle with pills and wrote a note—just in case. I didn’t go through with it, but the fact that I got that far… scares me. I don’t want to feel like this anymore.
D013_m008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m009.question:
I’ve just been feeling… heavy, for about two months now. It started slowly—just not looking forward to work, even though I’ve always been good at it. Being a nurse on the psych ward, I’m used to stress, but now I can’t seem to shake this constant sadness. Some days I cry in the parking lot before my shift, and I haven’t had the energy to explain care plans clearly to patients. That’s not like me.

I sleep, sometimes too much—eight, nine hours—but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t sleep at all. My brain feels foggy. I keep forgetting where I put things—my keys, patient charts—and I can’t focus during handoffs. I’ve started doubting myself, wondering if I’m even safe to practice.

The worst part? I catch myself thinking, *I wish I wouldn’t wake up tomorrow.* Not because I want to do anything to myself—just… the thought of not being here feels easier than this weight I carry every day. I’ve stopped calling friends, canceled plans with my son. I used to cook, garden—now I just stare at the wall. I don’t know how much longer I can keep going like this.
D013_m009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m010.question:
Lately, things just feel… heavy. It’s been about two months now where I can’t remember waking up feeling okay. I cry a lot—sometimes for no real reason. I’ll just start tearing up while sitting on the couch or even in the middle of sending a job application. It’s embarrassing, but I can’t stop it.

I sleep, like, eight hours most nights, but I still feel exhausted. My body’s tired, my mind’s foggy—it’s like I didn’t sleep at all. It’s messing with everything. I used to be able to focus when reading articles or watching something, but now I’ll look up and realize I was staring at the screen for 20 minutes and didn’t absorb a thing. Job searching feels impossible. I’ll open my laptop and then just sit there, overwhelmed, losing track of time.

Honestly, some days I think I’d just be better off gone. Not like I’m planning anything—I don’t want to scare anyone—but the thought of not waking up… it’s kind of comforting. I’ve never felt this disconnected before. It’s like I’m watching my life from far away, and I can’t reach it.
D013_m010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m011.question:
Lately… I mean, for about the past ten months or so, things just feel heavy. I don’t know how else to put it. I’ll be working my shift—walking the server rows, checking logs—and outta nowhere, I’ll start tearing up. I have to hide it, obviously, step into a back room or bathroom. It’s embarrassing. My boss hasn’t said anything, but I can tell I’m slipping. I used to enjoy the quiet of the night shift, but now I just… go through motions.

My head feels tired all the time, like my brain is full of static. Even simple things—like deciding which rack to troubleshoot first or reading an error report—take so much effort. I just don’t care anymore. I used to build PCs on the side, but now I can’t even bring myself to open a ticket at work if it’s not urgent.

Some days, I can’t even pick what to eat. I’ll stand in front of the fridge or the gas station cooler for ten minutes, just frozen. Should I get the sandwich or the wrap? Does it even matter? Nothing tastes good anyway. I’ve been calling out sick more often—not because I’m physically ill, just… empty. I don’t know how much longer I can keep this up.
D013_m011.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m012.question:
I’ve been feeling... nothing, really, for about ten months now. It started gradually—just a heaviness at work, maybe being a little tired. But now it’s like I’m moving through fog. I’m a social worker, so I spend my days trying to hold space for other people’s pain, but lately I can’t even access my own emotions, let alone theirs. It’s like I’m disconnected, numb. I used to love meeting new clients, coming up with plans, seeing progress—but now, even things I once enjoyed, like painting or going for walks in the park, feel pointless.

Concentrating has become so hard. I’ll read the same sentence in a case file three times and it won’t stick. I forget where I put my keys, my coffee cup, even basic words mid-sentence. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I used to be sharp—reliable. Now I’m calling myself names, wondering if I’m failing the people who need me. I live alone, and some weeks I don’t see anyone outside of work. I don’t call friends. I just don’t have the energy, mentally or emotionally. It feels like my brain is exhausted just from trying to function.
D013_m012.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m013.question:
I’ve just been going through the motions for about ten months now. I can’t even tell you when it started exactly—maybe after my youngest started school—but it hasn’t let up. I used to find so much joy in little things, like baking with the kids or meeting up with other moms, but now everything feels… flat. I don’t cry much, which is strange—I just feel empty, like I’m watching my life from far away.

Some days, just getting out of bed feels impossible. My body is so heavy, like I’m dragging bricks with every step. I shower when I have to, but even folding laundry wears me out. The house is messier than I ever thought I’d let it get.

I’ve stopped answering texts from friends. They invite us to playdates or girls’ nights, and I make excuses. It’s not that I don’t love them—I just can’t face talking, pretending I’m okay. My husband says I seem distant, and he’s right. I want to connect, but it’s like there’s a wall.

And my memory—honestly, I’ll stand in the kitchen wondering why I walked in, or I lose my keys three times a day. I worry I’m slipping, but I know it’s because my mind just can’t focus anymore. I love my kids, I love my family, but I feel so stuck.
D013_m013.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m014.question:
Lately, it’s been almost a year—maybe 10 months now—where nothing really feels like it matters. I wake up and just stare at the ceiling for a while, sometimes crying without even knowing why. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I run my own crypto trades, so no one sees me most days, but even logging into my accounts feels like climbing a mountain. The market could be crashing or booming, and I just… don’t care. I used to get excited when I made a solid return, but now, even when I hit a big win, it feels hollow.

Some days, I can’t even get off the couch. My apartment’s a mess, and I miss entries or leave orders unattended. I’ve started forgetting things—simple stuff, like where I put my phone or if I even ate. I’ll check my wallet balance three times because I can’t remember what it was. It’s not the trading that’s hard anymore—it’s the *wanting* to do anything at all. I used to be sharp, always on top of things. Now I feel like I’m moving through fog. I don’t call friends. I don’t answer my family. I just… exist.
D013_m014.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m015.question:
I’ve just been feeling so heavy lately—this sadness that doesn’t go away, no matter what I do. It’s been like this for about ten months now. I cry all the time, sometimes over nothing. At first, I thought it was just stress from work or being alone since my divorce, but it’s more than that. I’m tired—so tired—even when I’ve slept enough. Some mornings, I don’t even want to get up. It takes everything just to get dressed and make it to the bank.

At work, I’m struggling. I count the same bills over and over because I can’t focus. My manager said I’ve been slow, and I know I’m letting people down. I used to enjoy chatting with customers, but now I just want to be invisible. After work, I go straight home. My sister calls, friends invite me out, but I don’t answer. It feels like I’m watching my life from far away.

I don’t feel like myself. I can’t concentrate on a TV show, I forget what people say mid-conversation, and I’ve stopped going to my niece’s birthday parties. I used to care so much about being reliable—now I can’t even take care of myself.
D013_m015.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m016.question:
I’ve just turned 59, and for the past year and a half, everything’s felt… heavy. I used to take pride in my work—overseeing policy initiatives, managing teams—but now, a promotion came through last quarter, and I didn’t even care. It felt like nothing mattered. My staff noticed I’ve been quieter in meetings, and honestly, it’s hard to get the words out sometimes. I’ll be asked a question and just… pause. Not because I don’t know the answer, but because it takes so long to feel like speaking at all.

At home—well, I live alone—nights are the worst. I lie down at 10, but sleep doesn’t come until 2 or 3, if at all. My mind races over small things: a missed email, a comment I made years ago, things I can’t control. I keep thinking I’ve let people down—my team, my sister, even strangers on the subway. Like I’ve done something unforgivable just by existing. I don’t know why I can’t pull myself together. I used to be strong, capable. Now I feel like I’m failing at everything, even breathing. It’s exhausting. I can’t remember the last time I laughed.
D013_m016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m017.question:
I’ve just… stopped caring, really, for over a year now—about work, people, everything. I used to be on top of every case, every detail, but now I can’t even bring myself to open my briefs. I’ll sleep for 12, 13 hours and still feel like I’m dragging through mud. Some days, I don’t even get out of bed until after noon, and even then, it’s only because my paralegal calls three times.  

My colleagues notice. They invite me to lunch, to meetings, even just to grab coffee—small things I’d normally shrug off, but now I just say no. Not because I’m busy. I’m just… empty. Talking feels exhausting. I know I pause too long when people ask questions. I see them waiting, and I want to respond, but the words don’t come fast, if at all.  

And the guilt—God, the guilt—is unbearable. I keep thinking my divorce ruined my daughter’s life. She changed schools, yes, but she’s doing fine now. Still, I feel responsible for every bad thing that’s happened to her—even her car breaking down last winter. I know, logically, it doesn’t make sense… but in my mind, it’s proof. Every misstep, every hardship in her life now is my fault. Like I poisoned everything just by existing.
D013_m017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m018.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about a year and a half now—maybe longer, I don’t even track time the same anymore. Ever since things started fading at work, like not caring if I messed up the inventory or showing up late, which isn’t like me. I used to take pride in being reliable, especially working nights—it’s quiet, you keep things running. But now, I just go through the motions. Stocking shelves takes forever. I don’t call my friends anymore. Don’t answer my mom’s texts. What’s the point? Nothing feels meaningful. Even small tasks—tying my shoes—feel like they take effort they didn’t before. I’m still showing up to work, but barely. I don’t know how much longer I can keep this up.
D013_m018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m019.question:

I love my job—used to love it—but now it all just feels pointless. I don’t want to burden my husband, but I can’t seem to pull myself out of this.
D013_m019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m020.question:
I’ve been feeling… heavy, for over a year now—like every morning I’m wading through mud just to get dressed. Work’s getting harder. I’m an electrician’s apprentice, so I’m usually on my feet all day, running conduit, pulling wire—but lately, my body just feels sluggish. I move slower, drop tools, forget simple things. My boss said I’m not myself.

It’s not just the physical stuff, though. I don’t feel anything anymore. I used to love working on cars with my dad, or just hanging out with my crew after a job, cracking jokes. Now, nothing feels good. Not video games, not even seeing my little sister’s smile. It’s like I’m numb.

And the dreams—man, they’re brutal. I keep dreaming I’m standing in front of a burning building, people screaming inside, and I *know* it’s my fault. I didn’t start the fire, but in the dream, I did something—wired something wrong, left a live circuit ungrounded. I wake up sweating, heart going a hundred, and then I can’t go back to sleep.

I don’t know... sometimes I wonder if bad things happen because of me—like that car crash last month downtown. I wasn’t anywhere near it, but I keep thinking: what if I messed up somewhere that day? Left a junction box loose on a job site? Could that have caused a power surge, a light to fail… and caused that wreck? It sounds crazy, but I can’t shake it.
D013_m020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m021.question:

D013_m021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m022.question:
I’ve been feeling... empty, I guess. For over a year now—maybe a year and a half. It started around the time I turned 62. I still go to work most days, but it’s a struggle. I’m a security guard—night shift—used to be okay, but now the hours just drag, and I don’t care about much. 

I wake up every morning around 3:30 or 4 AM, wide awake, heart pounding. Can’t get back to sleep, so I just lie there, staring. Even when I’m off, I can’t rest. My wife says I’m not the same. Little things feel impossible now—what to eat, what shirt to wear. I stand there frozen, like my mind’s stuck. I’ve even thought about not being here anymore. I haven’t done it, but... the thought is always there. I don’t want to hurt my wife, but I don’t know how to fix this. I just feel broken.
D013_m022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D013_m023.question:
